title: Rigveda 1.97: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.97: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.97 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 68r-68v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.97.1-3 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 7, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 68r
translation.original_text:
1apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham agne̍ śuśu̱gdhy ā ra̱yim | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham ||
2su̱kṣe̱tri̱yā su̍gātu̱yā va̍sū̱yā ca̍ yajāmahe | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham ||
3pra yad bhandi̍ṣṭha eṣā̱m prāsmākā̍saś ca sū̱raya̍ḥ | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham ||
translation.text:
1CHASING with light our sin away, O Agni, shine thou wealth on us. May his light chase our sin away.
2For goodly fields, for pleasant homes, for wealth we sacrifice to thee. May his light chase our sin away.
3Best praiser of all these be he; foremost, our chiefs who sacrifice. May his light chase our sin away.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 68r (OPenn image 69, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.96.3 ‹-bharatam sṛpra-dānum devāḥ agnim›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 68v, begins in RV 1.97.4 ‹-śośucat agham›. Verses 1.97.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham | agne | śuśugdhi | ā | rayim | apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham
2su-kṣetriyā | sugātu-yā | vasu-yā | ca | yajāmahe | apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham
3pra | yat | bhandiṣṭhaḥ | eṣām | pra | asmākāsaḥ | ca | sūrayaḥ | apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham

translation.original_ref: RV 1.97.4-8 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 7, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 68v
translation.original_text:
4pra yat te̍ agne sū̱rayo̱ jāye̍mahi̱ pra te̍ va̱yam | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham ||
5pra yad a̱gneḥ saha̍svato vi̱śvato̱ yanti̍ bhā̱nava̍ḥ | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham ||
6tvaṁ hi vi̍śvatomukha vi̱śvata̍ḥ pari̱bhūr asi̍ | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham ||
7dviṣo̍ no viśvatomu̱khāti̍ nā̱veva̍ pāraya | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham ||
8sa na̱ḥ sindhu̍m iva nā̱vayāti̍ parṣā sva̱staye̍ | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cad a̱gham ||
translation.text:
4So that thy worshippers and we, thine, Agni, in our sons may live. May his light chase our sin away.
5As ever- conquering Agni's beams of splendour go to every side, May his light chase our sin away.
6To every side thy face is turned, thou art triumphant everywhere. May his light chase our sin away.
7O thou whose face looks every way, bear us past foes as in a ship. May his light chase our sin away.
8As in a ship, convey thou us for our advantage o'er the flood. May his light chase our sin away.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 68v (OPenn image 70, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.97.4 ‹-śośucat agham›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 69r, begins in RV 1.100.1 ‹-havyaḥ bhareṣu marutvān naḥ›. Verses 1.97.4-8 end on this page; 1.97.4 begins on fol. 68r.
translation.edition_text:
4pra | yat | te | agne | sūrayaḥ | jāyemahi | pra | te | vayam | apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham
5pra | yat | agneḥ | sahasvataḥ | viśvataḥ | yanti | bhānavaḥ | apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham
6tvam | hi | viśvataḥ-mukha | viśvataḥ | pari-bhūḥ | asi | apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham
7dviṣaḥ | naḥ | viśvataḥ-mukha | ati | nāvāiva | pāraya | apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham
8saḥ | naḥ | sindhum-iva | nāvayā | ati | parṣa | svastaye | apa | naḥ | śośucat | agham
